characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective of Baker Street; appears in disguises (out-of-work groom, Nonconformist clergyman).

characters.name: Dr. John Watson
characters.note: Narrator, Holmes's friend and chronicler; married, returned to medical practice.

characters.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, King of Bohemia
characters.note: Tall, imposing client in a mask and flamboyant dress; arrives incognito from Prague.

characters.name: Irene Adler
aliases: the slim youth in the ulster
characters.note: American-born contralto and adventuress; outwits Holmes; disguises herself as a young man.

characters.name: Godfrey Norton
characters.note: Lawyer of the Inner Temple; Irene Adler's suitor and husband.

characters.name: Clergyman of St. Monica's
characters.note: Priest who marries Irene Adler and Godfrey Norton, insisting on a witness.

characters.name: Mary Jane
characters.note: Watson's clumsy servant girl, mentioned only.

characters.name: Clotilde Lothman von Saxe-Meningen
characters.note: Scandinavian princess betrothed to the King of Bohemia; never appears.

characters.name: Baker Street landlady
characters.note: Holmes's landlady who brings in the tray.

characters.name: Elderly woman at Briony Lodge
characters.note: Irene's elderly servant who greets the visitors on the final morning.

characters.name: Loafers and bystanders of Serpentine Avenue
characters.note: Hired accomplices staging the brawl; also the crowd crying 'Fire!'.

characters.name: The two guardsmen
characters.note: Soldiers flirting with a nurse-girl, drawn into the staged quarrel.

characters.name: The scissors-grinder
characters.note: Street tradesman with his wheel, part of the staged scene.

characters.name: Maid at Briony Lodge
characters.note: Irene's maid who opens the door and the window.

characters.name: John, the coachman
characters.note: Irene's coachman; sent by her to shadow Holmes.

locations.name: 221B Baker Street
locations.note: Holmes's rooms with seventeen steps, fireplace, gasogene and index.

locations.name: Briony Lodge
locations.note: Irene's bijou villa in St. John's Wood, with sitting-room, sliding recess behind the bell-pull.

locations.name: Serpentine Avenue, St. John's Wood
locations.note: Quiet but animated street where the staged brawl occurs.

locations.name: Church of St. Monica
locations.note: Where Irene and Godfrey Norton marry in haste.

locations.name: Serpentine Mews
locations.note: Stabling lane by Briony Lodge's garden wall; source of gossip.

locations.name: The Langham
locations.note: Hotel where the King stays as Count Von Kramm; mentioned only.

locations.name: Gross & Hankey's, Regent Street
locations.note: Jeweller's visited by Norton; mentioned only.

locations.name: The Temple
locations.note: Godfrey Norton's legal chambers; mentioned only.

locations.name: Charing Cross station
locations.note: Departure point for the Continent; mentioned only.

brief.era: Late Victorian London, March 1888; gaslight, hansom cabs and broughams, horse-drawn traffic.
brief.place: Holmes's Baker Street sitting-room (fireplace, armchairs, cigar case, spirit case and gasogene, index volumes, pink notepaper); Briony Lodge, a two-storey bijou villa in St. John's Wood with long ground-floor windows, a garden behind and a coach-house; the Church of St. Monica with an altar and side aisles; the mews lane; Serpentine Avenue at dusk with lit lamps.
brief.dress: Holmes: dressing gown, tweed suit, and disguises — shabby groom with inflamed face; amiable Nonconformist clergyman in broad black hat, baggy trousers, white tie. Watson: professional dress, top hat, stethoscope. The King: flamboyant foreign dress — astrakhan-trimmed coat, deep blue cloak lined with flame-coloured silk, flaming beryl brooch, fur-topped boots, black vizard mask, broad-brimmed hat. Irene Adler: lovely, elegant; later in male walking clothes. Clergyman surpliced at the wedding.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Cabinet photograph, chamois leather bag of gold and notes, emerald snake ring, plumber's smoke-rocket, sliding panel recess behind the bell-pull, gold watch, sovereign on a watch chain, brougham and landau carriages.
depiction_rules: Holmes's disguises should be shown as convincing transformations, not obvious costumes.
Irene Adler in the final scene appears disguised as a slim youth in an ulster.
The King wears his mask until he tears it off; show the mask in early scenes.
The staged street brawl is theatre: all participants are accomplices.
No violence beyond the staged scuffle; the fire is a false alarm with smoke only.
